jobs: select an item by its id
rewrite the page address for the selection
summary: Takes an item id, or an empty value to clear the selection, and does nothing when the host is missing or the item is already selected. Otherwise it stores the id and runs the address sync with a flag set, so the sync replaces the current address entry instead of adding one.

jobs: list local storage keys and database stores
summary: Takes no input and returns one item for each local storage key, followed by one item for each object store in each database. Each item carries a prefixed id, a title and a meta line.

jobs: expand a database into its object stores
summary: Takes one database entry and returns an item for each of its object stores, for the surrounding list to flatten into one sequence.

jobs: describe an object store as a list item
summary: Takes an object store and its database and returns an item with a prefixed id, a title joining both names, and a meta line giving the record count. When the view shows a page and the store holds more than 500 records, the meta line says only the first 500 are shown.

jobs: give an item's file name and text
summary: Takes a list item and returns an object with a file name and text. Page items go to the page reader, local storage keys go to the helper that shows them, and database stores return their rows as indented JSON under a name made from the database and store names.

jobs: read the rows of a database store
summary: Takes a store item and returns its records as an array of rows, reading the entries from the database and converting them to rows. Results are kept per store until the source changes, and a read that fails gives an empty array, which is kept as well.

jobs: load nearby items into their panels
summary: Takes no input and works on the item in view and the items on either side of it. Each one not yet loaded gets a content viewer in its panel, filled with that item's content, and items already loaded are skipped.

jobs: find the card nearest the strip's left edge
summary: Returns the index of the card the strip is scrolled closest to, counted in whole card widths. Returns -1 when the strip has no width, as when it is hidden.

jobs: limit the scroll check to one per frame
summary: Takes no input and queues at most one check of the strip's position for the next animation frame. Scroll events that arrive while a check is queued do nothing.

jobs: follow the scroll to the card in view
load the viewers near the card
summary: Runs a frame after the strip scrolls, and while a programmatic move is still under way it waits until the strip reaches its target, so cards passed on the way do not change the selection. Otherwise it selects the nearest card if it differs from the current one, reveals it in the list, and loads the viewers around it.

jobs: move the view to an item by index
summary: Takes an item index and an optional instant flag, clamps the index to the list, then selects that item, reveals it in the list and scrolls the strip to its card. Does nothing when the list is empty.

jobs: scroll to the item in view once laid out
summary: Takes a retry count, six by default, and on the next frame scrolls the strip without animation to the item in view and loads its neighbors. If the strip has no width yet, it retries 50 ms later with one retry used up, and gives up waiting once the retries run out.

jobs: scroll to the item in view once laid out
summary: Runs on the frame after the jump starts. If the strip still has no width and retries remain, it schedules another attempt 50 ms later; otherwise it scrolls to the item in view without animation and loads its neighbors.

jobs: scroll the strip to a card
summary: Takes a card index and an instant flag, and scrolls the strip so that card fills the view, smoothly unless instant is set. The target is recorded as in flight so the scroll check ignores cards passed on the way, with a 900 ms fallback that releases it, and if the strip already sits on the card it only loads the neighboring viewers.

jobs: scroll the list to show the selected row
summary: Takes no input. On the next render it scrolls the list only as far as needed to bring the selected row inside its visible area, with a small margin at the top and bottom.

jobs: scroll the list to show the selected row
summary: Runs after render and does nothing unless the list is shown and holds the selected row. It moves the list's scroll position by the least amount that keeps the row at least 4 px inside each edge.

jobs: open the items as a full-screen deck
summary: Takes no input. If the list has items and no deck is open, it loads the swipe deck kit and opens an immersive full-screen deck that starts on the item in view, with each slide showing that item's content. Closing the deck returns the list to the item the deck last showed.

jobs: fill a deck slide with an item's content
summary: Takes a slide index and its element. It adds a padded, full-size container to the slide, mounts a content viewer in it, and loads that item's content into the viewer as local content.

jobs: clean up after the deck closes
summary: Takes no input. It forgets the open deck and the item it showed, then after 60 ms hands over to the step that selects that item once the host has finished restoring its address.

jobs: select the deck's item once the address settles
summary: Takes a retry count, twenty by default, and waits 50 ms at a time while the host is still restoring its address. Once it is settled, it selects the item and, after the next render, scrolls the strip to that item and reveals it in the list.

jobs: track the item the deck is showing
summary: Takes the index of the slide now showing. If an item exists at that index, it becomes the deck's current item and the deck's title and subtitle change to match.

jobs: switch the view to this browser's storage
list local storage keys with their sizes
list database stores with record counts
summary: Takes no input. It clears cached rows and loaded viewers, then reads every local storage key with its size in bytes (two per UTF-16 code unit), the storage usage and quota, and the databases with their stores and record totals. Any part the browser refuses leaves a plain message in its place, and the view then scrolls to the item in view.

jobs: ask the linked page a storage question
summary: Takes a read request and sends it over the page link to the page the reader opened the bookmark on, which runs a storage script with that request; the reply comes back parsed from JSON. Throws a plain instruction to tap the bookmark on a page when no page is linked.

jobs: switch the view to a linked page's storage
ask the page for its storage inventory
explain a page's refusal in plain words
summary: Takes no input. It clears cached rows and loaded viewers, makes the linked page the source, and asks the page for its storage inventory; if the page refuses, it shows a plain reason, naming the page's content security policy when that is the cause. A reply that arrives after the reader has moved to another source is dropped.

jobs: give a page item's file name and text
show a stored token's last four characters
return a page store's rows as JSON
summary: Takes a list item from the linked page and returns a file name and text. A value that looks like an access token shows only its last four characters, a stored object or array is pretty-printed, other values are shown as they are, and a failed read becomes a text note saying the page did not answer.

jobs: define the call card's color and icon tables
split a pull request reference into parts
open the call card's markup
summary: Declares the shared color tables, change-kind labels, step drawings and the two commentary figures, along with a helper that reads a pull request reference into its repository, number and label. It then opens the card's markup with the question, the merge status line and the verdict circle, and stops partway through the markup, where the next part continues it.

jobs: lay out the call card's question and views
show the merge status and warning lines
summary: Continues the card's markup with the merge status line, the brief with its pull request chip, and the tabs that switch the question between its diagram, plain words, questions, on-air lines and commentary dialogue. It also adds the blocker and recommendation lines, the link that opens a documentation call's edits for review, and the first part of the answer buttons.

jobs: lay out the answer and note controls
show each shipped change with its proof
summary: Continues the card's markup with the rest of the answer row, the note box with its post-to-pull-request option and send button, and the merge detail that lists each shipped change with its kind mark, old and new text, and proof chip. It also adds the message-instead-of-merge box, the answered history, the verdict menu and the pull request panel, and opens the materials section.

jobs: lay out the swipeable materials section
export the card's helpers and register the component
summary: Finishes the markup with the materials header, a swipeable strip of slides for each material, the notes and the adjustment form, and the commentary bubble. It then puts the link, pull request, answer, preview and branch helpers on the window, and registers the component now if the component system is ready or when it signals ready.

jobs: get or create a file's preview record
summary: Takes a repository, ref, path, file kind and address, and returns one shared, observable record for that file at that ref, creating it on first request. The record starts with no HTML, which a later step fills in.

jobs: fetch a file and render it as HTML
summary: Takes a preview record and fills its HTML once: it fetches the file from its repository, shows plain text escaped inside a preformatted block, and renders Markdown with the Markdown parser after the chat renderer has loaded. Pages are skipped, a record is asked for only once, and a failed fetch leaves the HTML empty rather than raising.

jobs: turn a typed link into a display target
summary: Takes a typed link (pull request, branch, file, task, app view or card) and a function that gives a pull request's state, and returns where the link goes with its label, icon and tint. Files, tasks and app views also get a preview record, and an app view carries over the page's own use setting and hides the app's chrome.

jobs: read a pull request's state and checks
summary: Takes a pull request reference and returns its facts: state (merged, closed, draft or open), a one-word check summary, mergeability, file and line counts, title, link, commits, last update and branch. A reference that does not parse gives null, and checks that cannot be read leave the check summary empty rather than failing the lookup.

jobs: append an answer line to a repo file
comment the answer on a pull request
summary: Takes an answer entry, a file path on a branch, and optionally a pull request with a comment. It fills in the author's login if missing, posts the comment first when asked and records its link on the entry, then appends the entry as one JSON line, re-reading and retrying up to three times if the write conflicts, and returns the entry.

jobs: open a set of branches as a deck
summary: Takes a list of branches, each with a repository, branch name and optional pull request, and a start index, and opens them as a full-screen swipe deck. Each slide shows its branch's brief, or its files or guide pane when the caller passes a pane option, and the branch kits load first; an empty list or a missing deck kit does nothing.

jobs: fill a branch slide with its brief
summary: Takes a slide index and its element and mounts the branch brief in it, with the branch's repository, branch, pull request and any requested pane as its settings. The settings sit on the window under a key of their own, which is removed when the slide is released.

jobs: update the deck header for the branch shown
summary: Takes the index of the slide now showing and sets the deck's title, subtitle, icon and link to that branch. It does nothing until the deck handle is available.

jobs: register the call form component
summary: Takes no input and registers the call form's data component under its name with the component system. It runs once that system is ready.

jobs: hold the call form's state and derived values
load the glossary, views and decision tree
mark glossary terms so a click pins a note
summary: Sets up the component's starting state and its computed values: the pull request, the answer options, the Take or Adjust mode, the materials list and the full-screen button. It also gives the answer buttons their styling, loads the glossary, question views and decision tree from their files, and marks glossary terms so that a click on one pins and shows its note.

jobs: handle clicks, tabs and proofs in the card
send an answer and keep its history
move the materials strip
summary: Continues the component's object with the handlers for clicks, keys, tabs, proof links, the answer summary and the lifecycle hooks, plus the header, verdict circle, pull request panel, full-screen materials and answer-sending helpers. Several of these members are only named in this part, so their bodies are not described here.

jobs: list a call's materials with shipped proofs
summary: Takes no input and returns a copy of the call's materials, with the proof of each shipped change added at the end unless the same file or page is already listed. Each entry is a link record.

jobs: order the materials into swipe slides
summary: Returns the slides for the materials strip, each a material link tagged with its source, key and answer. For a Take or Adjust call the Take materials lead, then the notes, the other materials and the Adjust form when it can be used; for other calls the notes come first, then a slide for each answer that names one, then the rest.

jobs: choose the full-screen button's look
summary: Takes no input and returns the icon, class and tooltip for the full-screen button in the materials header. Once the deck kit is ready it uses the kit's own entry, including its count-based label, and until then a plain card icon with a fixed tooltip.

jobs: pick an answer and show its slide
summary: Takes an answer label and toggles it as the picked answer, so tapping the picked one again clears it. Picking an answer that has a slide also moves the strip to that slide, and picking Adjust focuses its text box after a short delay; nothing changes while answering is unavailable or a send is busy.

jobs: style an answer button by its state
summary: Takes an answer label and returns its button classes: once an answer has been sent, the one that stands gets a success tint and the others fade. Otherwise a picked answer gets a primary tint, and the recommended answer (Take, in a Take or Adjust call) is outlined in primary while the rest keep a plain border.

jobs: load the glossary once
summary: Takes no input and returns one shared promise for reading the call's glossary, so the file is fetched at most once. The promise settles after the glossary's terms and step kinds are set on the form.

jobs: read the glossary's terms and step kinds
summary: Fetches and parses the glossary file the call names, keeping the entries that have terms, a question, an aside and either a home on this form or a link, plus the named step kinds. A call with no glossary does nothing, and a read that fails is logged as a warning and leaves the call unmarked.

jobs: load the question views once
summary: Takes no input and returns one shared promise for reading the call's views file, so it is fetched at most once. A file that cannot be read leaves the diagram and the plain words in place.

jobs: read the call's alternative views
summary: Fetches and parses the views file the call names into the form's views. A call that names no file does nothing, and a failed read is logged as a warning.

jobs: list the tabs for the question
summary: Takes no input and returns the question's tabs in order: diagram and in words always, then questions, on air and the commentary dialogue only where the views file supplies them. The dialogue tab is labeled with the two commentators' names.

jobs: pick the commentary for the slide showing
summary: Takes no input and returns the commentary lines from the views file that belong to the slide in view. It returns none while the reader is typing an adjustment or has a note pinned, so the commentary stays out of the way.

jobs: build a jump button for a material
summary: Takes a material and returns the markup for a small icon button, labeled with the material's name, that moves to that material's slide. The label is escaped before it is written into the markup.

jobs: render the decision tree with its links
summary: Fetches the call's decision tree, renders it with the glossary's terms marked, and adds a jump button beside each material whose field names a decision or one of its attributes. If the tree cannot be read, the form records a reason and falls back to the plain question.

jobs: turn a decision tree into markup
summary: Takes a parsed decision tree and returns its markup: the goal as a filled pill, with its decisions beneath it, each step drawn with its kind's icon and a tooltip from the kinds list. The text is escaped before it is written.

jobs: render a decision's lines and child decisions
summary: Takes a decision and returns the markup for the lines beneath it (its inquiry, the instrument for that inquiry, and any path not taken) followed by its child decisions in a nested list joined by branch lines. Returns nothing when the decision has neither a line nor a child.

jobs: render one decision as a pill
summary: Takes a decision and returns its pill, which lists the paths it offers by letter and name: an open decision gets the warning tint, and a closed one a faded tint with a settled icon. The decision this call asks is ringed, and the decision's own lines and children follow the pill.

jobs: mark glossary terms in a line of text
summary: Takes a line of text and returns it as escaped HTML with the glossary's terms marked, when a glossary and the term marker are both available. Otherwise it returns the escaped text unchanged.

jobs: make marked terms focusable with a visible bullet
summary: Takes a container element and, for each marked term inside it, makes the term keyboard-focusable and adds a small bullet after its text that darkens on hover. Returns the same element.

jobs: show the note for a term
summary: Takes a term's id, or nothing to clear, and sets that term's note on display and lights its mentions in the card. When the notes slide is showing, it also scrolls the note into view after the next render.

jobs: list the glossary terms the card mentions
summary: Returns the glossary entries that the card's tree, question and brief mention, in order of first mention and without repeats. The list is kept until the glossary or the tree changes.

jobs: scroll a note into view on its slide
summary: Takes a note's id and scrolls the notes slide only as far as needed to show that note, keeping 72 px clear at the foot for the floating button. Does nothing when the note is not on the slide.

jobs: bring the notes slide to the pinned note
summary: Takes no input. If the materials strip is not on the notes slide, it moves there first, and once the strip has arrived it scrolls the pinned note into view; a card with no notes does nothing.

jobs: pin a note from a click
summary: Takes a click event in the notes. Unless the click lands on a link, a click on a marked term pins that term's note and a click on a note row pins that row, or unpins it if it is already pinned; other clicks do nothing.

jobs: act on a click in the call card
summary: Takes a click in the card. A jump button goes to its material, a marked term pins its note and opens the notes, and a click on plain text outside any button, link, input or label clears the pinned note.

jobs: step to the next or previous note
summary: Takes a direction, positive for next and negative for previous, and moves through the card's notes in order, wrapping at either end. It pins the note reached and brings the notes slide up; with no notes it does nothing.

jobs: switch the question to a view tab
summary: Takes a tab index, records it as the current view, and smoothly scrolls the question's view strip to that tab.

jobs: go to a material by its key
summary: Takes a material's key and moves the materials strip to the slide filed under it, closing the contents list first. Does nothing when no slide has that key.

jobs: show a change's proof in the materials
summary: Takes a shipped change and, when its proof has a slide in the materials strip, moves the strip to that slide and scrolls the materials section into view. A change with no matching slide does nothing.

jobs: report what blocks the merge
summary: Returns a plain warning sentence when the pull request is open and has failing checks or merge conflicts, and an empty string otherwise. An empty string also comes back when the facts are not yet read or the pull request is already merged or closed.

jobs: set up the call card when it mounts
route arrow keys and stray focus for the card
summary: Renders the card's markup into its element, loads its data, refreshes the verdict circle when the busy or answer state changes, and restarts the commentary when the slide changes. It also listens for arrow keys and for the window losing focus, so the keys step through the notes and a stray material frame hands focus back to the card.

jobs: step through notes with the arrow keys
summary: Takes a key press and, for an unmodified left or right arrow outside a text field, steps the notes back or forward when focus is in the card, or when the card is on its own page with no deck over it. It stands aside when the pointer or focus is in the materials, and when it acts it stops the key reaching other handlers and moves focus to the pinned term if a term had focus.

jobs: defer the focus check until after blur
summary: Takes no input and schedules the focus check to run once the current event ends, so the browser has finished moving focus before it is read.

jobs: return focus from a stray material frame
summary: If focus has moved into a material frame that is off the slide showing, or into one before the reader has clicked anything on the page, it blurs that frame and returns focus to the last element the reader focused in the card. Otherwise it does nothing.

jobs: attach arrow keys to the materials section
summary: Takes no input and connects the materials section to the shared swipe handler so arrow keys move through the materials, first releasing any earlier connection. It does nothing when the section or the handler is missing.

jobs: remove the card's global listeners
summary: Takes no input and removes the card's key listener, its focus listener and its materials key handling, so none keeps running after the card is gone.

jobs: load the call and its supporting files
report a call that cannot be opened
summary: Loads the guide renderer kit and the title tip kit, then fetches the call from its address when it was not given directly, and starts reading its answers, glossary, views and tree. It also loads the deck kit when needed, updates the header, and refreshes it with the pull request's facts; any failure shows a plain 'could not open this call' message.
